advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Stamp put_metric_data with a Timestamp derived from the log record times (or otherwise reconcile per-delivery aggregation with the 300s Sum threshold).
evidence: handler.py:72-82 _put_metric emits MetricData without a 'Timestamp' key
handler.py:93 counts are aggregated per S3 object and published per invocation
monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf:19-20 'Server access logs are delayed best-effort delivery, so this alarm detects the burst after delivery rather than at request time.'
monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf:174-176 period=300, threshold=5 evaluated as Sum over 300s
advisory.finding: The Lambda publishes the denial count via put_metric_data with no explicit Timestamp, so each datapoint is stamped at Lambda-invocation (log-delivery) time rather than the request time in the log records. Because S3 server access logs are delayed best-effort delivery (acknowledged in the header comment), a genuine denial burst split across multiple log objects delivered in different 300s windows is counted in separate windows, and each partial count can fall at or below the Sum>5 threshold — masking the burst the alarm exists to catch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a liveness signal (e.g. always publish a heartbeat/zero metric or a separate freshness metric) so a stalled Lambda or absent log delivery is distinguishable from a clean zero-denial result.
evidence: handler.py:67-69 _read_log_object calls s3.get_object with no try/except; an error propagates and skips _put_metric
handler.py:96-97 _put_metric only called when processed_objects>0
monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf:178 treat_missing_data = "notBreaching"
Litmus: the 'no denials' verdict is produced identically when the Lambda never ran, errored, or logs were never delivered
advisory.finding: Fail-open silent gap: the metric is only published when a log object is processed, and any get_object failure in _read_log_object raises and aborts the whole invocation before _put_metric runs. Combined with the alarm's treat_missing_data='notBreaching', a period with no delivered log objects, a Lambda permission/read error, or a stalled access-log delivery pipeline is indistinguishable from 'checked and zero unexpected denials' — the alarm stays OK whether the check ran clean or never ran at all.

The bucket is externally owned, referenced as a data source: `infra/terraform/monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf:42-44 data "aws_s3_bucket" "lmn_private_context_logs"`
ABSENCE: aws_s3_bucket_notification is the only such resource in the module (search_files) so Terraform cannot know about, and will not preserve, any out-of-band notification config on this bucket

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a CloudWatch Errors alarm (and/or DLQ) on the lmn-private-context-denied-metric Lambda so parser failures are visible.
evidence: infra/terraform/monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf:121-138 defines the Lambda with no dead_letter_config and no companion Errors alarm

advisory.finding: There is no alarm or dead-letter handling for the metric-producing Lambda itself, so if lmn-private-context-denied-metric fails (S3 read error, parse crash) or is never invoked, unexpected denials are silently under-reported and the alarm's treat_missing_data=notBreaching keeps it green.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a handler test with a non-matching bucket/prefix record asserting processed_objects=0 and no metric published.
evidence: handler.py:91-92 `if bucket != LOG_BUCKET or not key.startswith(LOG_PREFIX):` / `continue`

Named violating input: a Records entry with bucket='lmn-staging-private-context-896586841071' (the source bucket, not the log bucket) or key='logs/example.log' should yield processed_objects=0 and no put_metric_data call, but the added guard is never driven by any test.
test only sends bucket='lmn-staging-private-context-logs-896586841071', key='access/example.log' (test_lmn_private_context_denied.py:116-118)
handler.py:96-97 `if processed_objects:` / `_put_metric(unexpected_denials)`

Named violating input: handler({"Records": []}, None) should leave fake.cloudwatch.metric_data == [] and return {"processed_objects": 0, "unexpected_denials": 0}, but no test asserts the suppress-publication branch.
Given the alarm uses treat_missing_data='notBreaching' (monitoring_lmn_private_context.tf), whether a 0 is published vs omitted is behaviorally significant.
handler.py:90 `key = unquote_plus(record.get("s3", {}).get("object", {}).get("key", ""))`

Named violating input: key='access%2Fexample.log' (or 'access/my+file.log') — S3 delivers URL-encoded keys; without decoding, prefix matching against 'access/' could break. Test uses plain 'access/example.log' (test_lmn_private_context_denied.py:118).
ABSENCE: no test feeds an encoded key, so removing unquote_plus would not fail any test.
advisory.finding: No test exercises the bucket/prefix filter guard: a record whose bucket != LOG_BUCKET or whose key does not start with 'access/' must be skipped (continue) and not counted. Only a matching record is ever fed to handler().
merged_from: No test covers the no-matching-records path: when processed_objects is 0 the handler must NOT call put_metric_data and must return {processed_objects: 0, unexpected_denials: 0}. This guard (lines 96-97) is untested.

The unquote_plus decoding of the S3 object key (line 90) is never exercised: the test supplies an already-decoded key 'access/example.log', so a URL-encoded key from a real S3 event notification is untested.
scenarios: S3 notification delivers an event for a non-matching key or bucket

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test feeding blank, unbalanced-quote, and short (<12 field) lines and asserting they are skipped without error.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the audit exclusion to the specific audit IAM role name (parts[1]), not just a caller-controllable session-name prefix, so denials cannot be self-suppressed by choosing a RoleSessionName.
evidence: handler.py:41-47: `parts = requester.split("/")` then returns true when `parts[0].startswith("arn:aws:sts::896586841071:assumed-role")` and `parts[2].startswith(AUDIT_SESSION_PREFIX)` — parts[1] (the role name) is never checked
assumed-role ARN form is `arn:aws:sts::ACCOUNT:assumed-role/ROLE/SESSION`, so parts[2] is the caller-chosen RoleSessionName supplied at sts:AssumeRole time
_is_unexpected_denial (handler.py:50-56) drops any record where `_is_audit_runner(record.requester)` is true, so a matched session name removes that denial from the counted total and from the alarm
advisory.finding: The audit-runner exclusion (_is_audit_runner) matches on the RoleSessionName only and does not constrain the IAM role name, so any principal able to assume any role in account 896586841071 can set RoleSessionName to 'lmn-staging-private-audit-*' and have its genuine 403 AccessDenied hits excluded from the alarm's count, suppressing the security signal.
scenarios: A compromised or misconfigured lower-privilege role in the account assumes a role and names its session 'lmn-staging-private-audit-attacker'; its repeated AccessDenied attempts against the private-context bucket are excluded and never trip the alarm.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _is_audit_runner, additionally require parts[1] to equal the known audit role name (e.g. the role the lmn-staging-private-audit runner assumes) rather than accepting any role whose session name starts with AUDIT_SESSION_PREFIX.

blocking.suggested_fix: Add `alarm_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]` (and likely `ok_actions = [aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn]`) to the alarm block, matching the sibling alarms.
